arxiv-2111-02646.title: Engaging Politically Diverse Audiences on Social Media
arxiv-2111-02646.creator: Martin Saveski, Doug Beeferman, David McClure, Deb Roy
arxiv-2111-02646.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Martin Saveski, Doug Beeferman, David McClure, Deb Roy. We study how political polarization is reflected in the social media posts used by media outlets to promote their content online. In particular, we track the Twitter posts of several media outlets over the course of more than three years (566K tweets), and the engagement with these tweets from other users (104M retweets), modeling the relationship between the tweet text and the political diversity of the audience.

arxiv-2112-14682.title: Exact quantum query complexity of computing Hamming weight modulo powers of two and three
arxiv-2112-14682.creator: Arjan Cornelissen, Nikhil S. Mande, Maris Ozols, Ronald de Wolf
arxiv-2112-14682.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Arjan Cornelissen, Nikhil S. Mande, Maris Ozols, Ronald de Wolf. We study the problem of computing the Hamming weight of an n n -bit string modulo m m , for any positive integer m ≤ n m\leq n whose only prime factors are 2 and 3. We show that the exact quantum query complexity of this problem is ⌈ n ⁡ ( 1 − 1 / m ) ⌉ \left\lceil n(1-1/m)\right\rceil .

arxiv-2201-00406.title: There are no Collatz m m -Cycles with m ≤ 91 m\leq 91
arxiv-2201-00406.description: Abstract The Collatz conjecture (or “Syracuse problem”) considers recursively-defined sequences of positive integers where n n is succeeded by n 2 \tfrac{n}{2} , if n n is even, or 3 ​ n + 1 2 \tfrac{3n+1}{2} , if n n is odd.

arxiv-2403-06004.title: Determining the Locating Rainbow Connection Number of Vertex-Transitive Graphs
arxiv-2403-06004.creator: Ariestha Widyastuty Bustan, A.N.M. Salman, Pritta Etriana Putri
arxiv-2403-06004.description: Abstract The locating rainbow connection number of a graph is defined as the minimum number of colors required to color vertices such that every two vertices there exists a rainbow vertex path and every vertex has a distinct rainbow code. This rainbow code signifies a distance between vertices within a given set of colors in a graph.

arxiv-2404-11649.title: Stark Many-Body Localisation Under Periodic Driving
arxiv-2404-11649.creator: Christian Duffin, Aydin Deger, Achilleas Lazarides
arxiv-2404-11649.description: Abstract We study stability of localisation under periodic driving in Stark many-body systems. We find that localisation is stable except near special resonant frequencies, where resonances cause delocalisation. We provide approximate analytical arguments and numerical evidence in support of these results.

arxiv-2406-10424.title: What is the Visual Cognition Gap between Humans and Multimodal LLMs?
arxiv-2406-10424.creator: Xu Cao, Yifan Shen, Bolin Lai, Wenqian Ye, Yunsheng Ma, Joerg Heintz, Jintai Chen, Meihuan Huang, Jianguo Cao, Aidong Zhang, James M. Rehg
arxiv-2406-10424.description: Abstract Recently, Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) and Vision Language Models (VLMs) have shown great promise in language-guided perceptual tasks such as recognition, segmentation, and object detection. However, their effectiveness in addressing visual cognition problems that require high-level multi-image reasoning and visual working memory is not well-established.

arxiv-2409-17048.title: Predictive Covert Communication Against Multi-UAV Surveillance Using Graph Koopman Autoencoder Thanks: † S. Krishnan and J. Choi are with the School of Information Technology, Deakin University, Australia. Thanks: ∗ J. Park is with the Information Systems Technology and Design pillar, Singapore Univ
arxiv-2409-17048.creator: Sivaram Krishnan, Jihong Park, Gregory Sherman, Benjamin Campbell, Jinho Choi
arxiv-2409-17048.description: Abstract Low Probability of Detection (LPD) communication aims to obscure the presence of radio frequency (RF) signals to evade surveillance. In the context of mobile surveillance utilizing unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), achieving LPD communication presents significant challenges due to the UAVs’ rapid and continuous movements, which are characterized by unknown nonlinear dynamics.

europmc-pmc7272632.creator: Kanaan NM, Hamel C, Grabinski T, Combs B.
europmc-pmc7272632.description: Formation of membrane-less organelles via liquid-liquid phase separation is one way cells meet the biological requirement for spatiotemporal regulation of cellular components and reactions. Recently, tau, a protein known for its involvement in Alzheimer's disease and other...

pmc-10526774.title: In Search of Disentanglement in Tandem Mass Spectrometry Datasets
pmc-10526774.creator: Krzysztof Jan Abram, Douglas McCloskey
pmc-10526774.description: Generative modeling and representation learning of tandem mass spectrometry data aim to learn an interpretable and instrument-agnostic digital representation of metabolites directly from MS/MS spectra. Interpretable and instrument-agnostic digital representations would facilitate comparisons of MS/MS spectra between instrument vendors and enable better and more accurate queries of large MS/MS spectra databases for metabolite identification.

pmc-11341864.title: Motivators and mechanisms for an international rural health collaboration
pmc-11341864.creator: Neil J. MacKinnon, Melissa Powell-Williams, Preshit Nemdas Ambade, Vanessa Emery, Puja Punukollu, Merry Chen
pmc-11341864.description: Collaborations are critical to address rural health challenges. We evaluated a new international collaboration between institutions in Georgia, the United States (US), and Scotland, United Kingdom (UK), to address rural health issues and to understand the barriers and facilitators to effective international collaboration efforts.

pmc-11477327.title: Whole-Genome Sequences of 13 Chinese Indigenous Pinewood Nematodes, Bursaphelenchus xylophilus
pmc-11477327.creator: Bo Dong, Hao Wu, Debin Li, Zaiquan Luo, Shan He, Xin Hao, Junxin Gao
pmc-11477327.description: The pinewood nematode (Bursaphelenchus xylophilus, PWN) induces pine wilt disease in Pinaceae plants, causing severe destruction to pine forests. Previous studies report that by 2023, 663 cities across 18 provinces in China had been infested by the PWN, necessitating immediate control measures.

pmc-11586683.title: Molecular Discovery of Filarial Nematode DNA in an Endangered Wild Pinniped (Galapagos Sea Lion, Zalophus wollebaeki)
pmc-11586683.creator: Isabella G Livingston, Taylor M Gregory, Eleanor C Hawkins, Ashley Cave, Andrea Loyola, Shelly L Vaden, Diane Deresienski, Marjorie Riofrío‐Lazo, Gregory A Lewbart, Diego Páez‐Rosas, Matthew Breen
pmc-11586683.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Rapidly changing environments are contributing to the spread of non‐native species and their associated pathogens into new and vulnerable ecosystems, such as the Galapagos archipelago. These pathogens represent a significant threat to emblematic species. The Galapagos sea lion ( Zalophus wollebaeki ) (GSL) is an endangered and endemic pinniped that is increasingly at risk of acquiring infectious diseases due to interactions with introduced companion animals.

pmc-11640617.title: Proteomic Analysis Reveals Cadherin, Actin, and Focal Adhesion Molecule-Mediated Formation of Cervical Cancer Spheroids
pmc-11640617.creator: Piyatida Molika, Kittinun Leetanaporn, Wararat Chiangjong, Pongsakorn Choochuen, Raphatphorn Navakanitworakul
pmc-11640617.description: Cancer spheroids are spherical, three-dimensional (3D), in vitro assemblies of cancer cells, which are gaining importance as a useful model in cancer behavior studies. Designed to simulate key features of the in vivo tumor microenvironment, spheroids offer reliable insights for drug screening and testing applications. We observed contrasting phenotypes in 3D cervical cancer (CC) cultures.

pmc-11693802.title: Male Breast Cancer Biology, Screening, Treatment, and Follow-Up: A Narrative Review
pmc-11693802.creator: Morteza Akbari, Hadi Nasiri, Mojtaba Ziaee
pmc-11693802.description: Male breast cancer (MBC) is a rare type of cancer that affects men, accounting for only 1% of all cancers in men and all breast cancer cases worldwide. Its rarity is due to the differences in male endocrine function and the smaller amount of mammary tissue in males.

pmc-12612600.title: Needle‐ and Canopy‐Level Genetic Variation in Scots Pine (Pinus sylvestris L.) Revealed by Hyperspectral Phenotyping Across Sites and Seasons
pmc-12612600.creator: Daniel Provazník, Jan Stejskal, Zuzana Lhotáková, Jaroslav Čepl, Eva Neuwirthová, Adenan Yandra Nofrizal, Jiří Korecký, Lucie Červená, Lucie Kupková, Jaroslav Klápště, Jon Kehlet Hansen, Salvador A. Gezan, Petya Campbell, Milan Lstibůrek, Jana Albrechtová
pmc-12612600.description: As an essential species across European forests, Scots pine ( Pinus sylvestris L.) plays a vital ecological and economic role, yet its physiological variability underlying its adaptive potential remains underexplored. Understanding this intraspecific variability is crucial for uncovering the genetic basis of adaptation.

pmc-12660249.title: Triglyceride-glucose index as a predictor of cardiovascular multimorbidity: a prospective cohort study
pmc-12660249.creator: Yushi Bao, Hao Chen, Bolin Zhu, Minhua Tang, Qiang Wu, Yingnan Jia, Yonggen Jiang
pmc-12660249.description: BackgroundThe triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index is a recognized marker of insulin resistance, yet its role in the dynamic progression from cardiovascular disease (CVD) to cardiovascular multimorbidity (CVM) remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the association between the TyG index and transitions from a CVD-free state to first CVD and subsequently to CVM.

pmc-13130965.title: An Integrated Approach Combining Regulatory Tests in tg(cyp19a1b:GFP) Zebrafish Embryos to Assess Toxicity, Developmental Effects, and Estrogenic Activity of Chemicals: A Case Study with Bisphenol A Substitutes
pmc-13130965.creator: Florian Geffroy, Armelle Christophe, Benjamin Piccini, Nathalie Hinfray, Edith Chadili, Emmanuelle Maillot-Marechal, Xavier Cousin, Mélanie Blanc-Legendre, Thierry D. Charlier, Pascal Pandard, Selim Aït-Aïssa, François Brion
pmc-13130965.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The use of efficient testing strategies for chemical hazard assessment is a current challenge in supporting regulatory requirements. Herein, we combined two zebrafish eleuthero-embryo assays, a refined Fish Embryo Acute Toxicity assay (FET, OECD TG 236) and the EASZY assay (OECD TG 250), both using transgenic tg­(cyp19a1b:GFP) embryos, to jointly assess acute toxicity, developmental effects, and estrogenic activity of bisphenol A (BPA) and ten substitutes.

pmc-13198633.title: Conversion of endoscopic nasobiliary drainage into internal drainage versus endoscopic biliary stenting for benign biliary obstruction: a retrospective propensity score-matched comparative study
pmc-13198633.creator: Yan Zhao, Yongqiu Wei, Junxiong Wang, Can Sun, Wenkun Li, Yongjun Wang, Peng Li, Wenhai Wang
pmc-13198633.description: Background:Endoscopic nasobiliary drainage (ENBD) conversion to internal drainage using scissor forceps is a specialized technique primarily explored in malignant obstructions. This study evaluates its efficacy, radiation safety, and long-term durability in patients with benign biliary obstruction (BBO) compared to conventional endoscopic retrograde biliary drainage (ERBD).

pmc-13487533.title: AI-integrated single-cell multi-omics decodes the hepatocellular carcinoma metabolism-immune axis: a new strategy for precision therapeutic targeting
pmc-13487533.creator: Zihao Xu, Yifan Liu, Liangbin Cheng, Jun Xu
pmc-13487533.description: BackgroundImmune checkpoint inhibitors have improved outcomes for hepatocellular carcinoma, yet most patients do not respond because the tumor’s metabolic environment suppresses immune cells. Single-cell RNA sequencing has revealed extensive immune diversity, but conventional analyses cannot link cell states to their physical location or to the metabolic signals that drive dysfunction.

pmc-13719175.title: A haplotype-resolved triploid genome assembly of Zingiber striolatum sheds light on genome expansion and trait evolution in Zingiberaceae
pmc-13719175.creator: Zhi-Feng Chen, Wei-Hong Sun, Li-Yao Su, Guo-Fei Tan, Yu Lu, Lian Luo, Wen-Hui Li, Chun-Xiao Li, Zi-Wei Tan, Zhuang Zhao, Chang-Ling Sui, Zhong-Jian Liu, Ai-Sheng Xiong
pmc-13719175.description: The genus Zingiber represents an economically important group within Zingiberaceae, distinguished by its aromatic and bioactive rhizomes. Zingiber striolatum Diels is an endemic Chinese medicinal and edible plant highly valued for its flower buds, which are rich in natural red pigments (yanghe red pigment, YRP).
